correctness.rationale: The four-secant Akima derivative is a nonnegative weighted mean whose weights satisfy an exact half-total-variation inequality. On monotone uniform-grid data this yields hm_i<=M/2 by telescoping. The cubic Hermite basis has only one negative derivative basis function, whose magnitude peaks at 4/27; the symmetric upper estimate is identical. An explicit rational family approaches the bound and an affine transform gives a strictly positive sign-reversal witness. The packaged checker returns VERIFY_OK.

broader_coverage.reasoning: These sources show that qualitative overshoot and monotonicity remedies are prior work. They do not determine the exact worst excursion of the unmodified uniform-grid Akima rule.

originality.rationale: The Akima construction, qualitative overshoot, and monotonicity-preserving alternatives are prior work and explicitly excluded. The accepted claim is the sharp 2/27 bounded-monotone-data range defect, the half-total-variation derivative lemma, the sharp family, and the strict-positive sign-reversal witness. residual_risks: The original Akima 1970 article was not recovered as verified full text, so a hidden explicit bound there cannot be ruled out from direct inspection.
Older engineering or computer-graphics literature may encode the same constant as an overshoot factor without using range-defect terminology.
The theorem is restricted to uniform grids; nonuniform Akima variants may have different sharp constants.

value.rationale: Original Akima interpolation is a widely used local cubic rule chosen to suppress visually objectionable oscillation, yet it is not monotonicity preserving. The exact 2/27 envelope supplies a sharp safety margin for bounded monotone data and the strict-positive witness shows direct relevance to physical positivity constraints. The result is structural and global over the full admissible class, not an arbitrary finite example.
